ov: A family of 96 species of small brown songbirds with short, barred wings and tails often held upright. All live in the Americas except the Eurasian wren, which is found across Europe, Asia and North Africa. Most are hard to see but have loud songs.
rg: The Americas, plus the Eurasian wren across Europe, Asia and North Africa.
df: Insects, spiders and other small invertebrates; some also eat plants, frogs and lizards.
fx: Its scientific name means "cave-dweller", from its habit of creeping into crevices.
The male Eurasian wren is highly polygynous, unusual for a songbird.
